findings.title: Bash command strings logged verbatim, bypassing repo secret scrubbing (CWE-532)
findings.why_it_matters: Any credential a session puts in a git-bearing command line lands in cleartext in a durable, never-rotated file that CONTRIBUTING itself tells operators to grep and that handsoff/bug-report workflows routinely quote. Verified empirically: `git -C <shared> push https://x-access-token:ghp_AAAA...@github.com/o/r HEAD` produced `... cmd=git -C ... push https://x-access-token:ghp_AAAABBBBCCCCDDDDEEEEFFFF1234567890ab@github.com/o/r HEAD` at mode 0644. The 160-byte truncation is not redaction — leading env assignments (`GH_TOKEN=...`) and credential-in-URL remotes both sit inside the first 160 bytes, which is precisely the shape the repo's own `secret_scrubber` exists to catch. This repo has a quotable rule (CONTRIBUTING.md:226 'Never log API keys or secrets') and a mechanism whose doc header states it redacts exactly this data class 'before it is written to the tool_calls table'; the guard persists the same Bash tool-call `command` input with no scrub. The bypass path at line 272 is materially wider than the deny path: it fires before T1-T4 are evaluated, so with `MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT=0` armed every command merely *containing* the substring `git` has its first 160 bytes persisted, including non-git commands (confirmed: `GH_TOKEN=ghp_SECRET... gh pr merge 1 && git log` was logged in full).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a shell `scrub_cmd()` helper mirroring the prefix set already enumerated in crates/mika-agent/src/secret_scrubber.rs (github_pat_/ghp_/gho_/ghs_/ghu_/sk-ant-/sk-proj-/sk-or-/gsk_/xoxb-/xoxp-, `*_{TOKEN,KEY,SECRET}=\S+`, and `://<user>:<pw>@`) and pipe `$command` through it at both call sites, scrubbing BEFORE truncating (truncate-then-scrub can leave a token prefix that no longer matches the regex but still leaks). Same one-place-only discipline as check-secrets.sh's SECRET_REGEX. Additionally create the log under `( umask 077; ... )` so the file is 0600 rather than 0644. Assumption: the shell-side pattern list is allowed to drift behind the Rust one; if that is unacceptable, log only `verb` + target + a SHA-256 of the command instead of the command text.
evidence: scripts/guard-shared-checkout:466 -- 		guard_log "deny project=$project_dir target=$toplevel verb=$verb cmd=${command:0:160}"

scripts/guard-shared-checkout:272 -- 		guard_log "bypass MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT=0 project=$project_dir cmd=${command:0:160}" (emitted before T1..T4 are evaluated, so it is not limited to the guarded population)
CONTRIBUTING.md:226 -- '- Never log API keys or secrets' (pre-existing rule; `git diff HEAD~1 -- CONTRIBUTING.md` shows this line is not introduced by the diff)

crates/mika-agent/src/secret_scrubber.rs:1-4 -- '//! Secret-shaped value scrubber for tool_calls persistence. //! Redacts known secret patterns (API keys, tokens, PEM private keys, env var //! assignments containing secrets) from arbitrary text before it is written to //! the `tool_calls` table.' — table includes `GH(_APP)?_TOKEN=\S+` and `ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]+`

Empirical, via `--decide` on a throwaway worktree pair: log line produced was `2026-09-18T22:08:42Z deny project=/tmp/.../wt target=/tmp/.../mika verb=push cmd=git -C /tmp/.../mika push https://x-access-token:ghp_AAAABBBBCCCCDDDDEEEEFFFF1234567890ab@github.com/o/r HEAD`; `ls -l` reported `-rw-r--r--`

CONTRIBUTING.md:80 -- 'grep shared-checkout-guard ~/.mika/state/shared-checkout-guard.log' — the log is a documented operator surface, i.e. content that gets read and pasted, not an internal temp file

findings.title: Wiring check gates presence, not absence, on a tracked auto-executing settings.json
findings.why_it_matters: This diff turns `.claude/settings.json` into a repo-tracked file that Claude Code executes before every Bash call of every collaborator, with no install step — that is the property the change is buying, and `check-shared-checkout-guard-wiring.sh` is the gate that is supposed to protect it. The gate only asserts the guard entry is *present* (`length > 0`) and that one single key, `permissions`, is *absent*. Nothing asserts the file contains nothing else. So a later commit can append a second `hooks` entry (any event, any command) and all three CI steps stay green while that command runs on every collaborator's machine; or it can add a top-level `env` block setting `MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT` to `0`, which line 271 of the guard reads as the derogation — disarming the guard fleet-wide from inside the very file the check is guarding, with the only trace being `bypass` lines in a log nobody is required to read. Tightening the check to an exact shape (allowed top-level keys, allowed hook events, and every `.command` equal to the single guard invocation) closes both, and matches the exact-match discipline the repo already applies in scripts/check-dispatch-seats-declared.sh, which compares two lists *both ways* rather than checking containment.
findings.suggested_fix: In check-shared-checkout-guard-wiring.sh, replace the two `length > 0` containment probes with exact-shape assertions: (a) `jq -e '[keys[]] | inside(["$comment","hooks"])'`, (b) `jq -e '[.hooks | keys[]] | inside(["PreToolUse","SessionStart"])'`, and (c) `jq -e --arg c "bash \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/guard-shared-checkout\"" '[.hooks[][].hooks[].command] | unique == [$c]'` so any extra command or event fails. Keep the existing `has("permissions")` check as-is (it is subsumed but names its own reason). Add the matching negative fixtures to scripts/test-check-shared-checkout-guard-wiring.sh — an extra PostToolUse hook and an `env` block — so the new assertions are themselves watched go red.
evidence:
scripts/check-shared-checkout-guard-wiring.sh:93-99 -- `if jq -e --arg g "$GUARD_REL" '
  (.hooks.PreToolUse // [])
  | map(select((.matcher // "") | test("Bash")))
  | map(.hooks // []) | add // []
  | map(select((.command // "") | contains($g)))
  | length > 0
' "$SETTINGS"` — `length > 0` admits any number of additional, unrelated hook entries
scripts/check-shared-checkout-guard-wiring.sh:122 -- `if jq -e 'has("permissions")' "$SETTINGS" >/dev/null 2>&1; then` — the only key the check denies; no allowlist bounds the rest
scripts/guard-shared-checkout:271 -- 		if [ "${MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT:-1}" = 0 ]; then — the disarm is a plain env read, so a settings-level `env` block reaches it

.claude/settings.json:11-14 -- the file's own `$comment` states the safety argument as key-disjointness ('Il ne porte QUE la clé \'hooks\''), which is asserted for `permissions` only and for no other key

residual_risks: Injection audit result (no finding): I traced every expansion that touches the model-authored command string — `normalize_path`'s `for part in $path` (guarded by `set -f` with a function-local `IFS='/'`), the token loop's `for raw in $line` (guarded by `set -f`, default IFS restored because `IFS= read` scopes to the read builtin only), every `case` subject (patterns are literals; `path_is_within` quotes `"$root"` inside the pattern), every array index (`idx`/`j`/`k`/`i` are internal counters, never input-derived, so the arithmetic context of `${arr[expr]}` is not reachable), and `${command:0:160}`. There is no `eval`, no `$( )` over input, no `read` without `-r`. Confirmed empirically: command-substitution, backtick, `$[ ]` arithmetic, glob and quoted-substitution payloads run through `--decide` created no side effect (`/tmp/PWNED_2107_*` absent after all five).

Silent disarm is reachable by anyone who controls the hook process's environment: `MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT=0` combined with a swallowed log write (guard_log:65 `2>/dev/null || true`) or with `MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT_LOG=/dev/null` leaves no trace at all. CONTRIBUTING.md:65 states the derogation is 'journalisée' without that condition, while CONTRIBUTING.md:94-96 documents the log fail-open — the operator-facing claim is stronger than the code. Not filed as a finding: the fail-open is an explicit, reasoned decision, and the same principal controls both the switch and the log. Note the derogation is NOT reachable from a Bash tool call — shell state does not persist into the harness-spawned hook process.

`guard_log_path` uses `MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT_LOG` verbatim with `mkdir -p -- "$dir"` and `>>"$path"`, and the default falls back to `${MIKA_HOME:-${HOME:-/tmp}/.mika}`. With `HOME` unset the log becomes a predictable 0644 path under world-writable `/tmp`, where another local user can pre-create the directory or symlink the file and receive the appends (CWE-59/CWE-377). `~/.mika` is 0700 on the measured host so the normal path is contained; I could not establish a deployment where `HOME` is unset for a Claude Code hook, so this is recorded rather than filed.

scripts/guard-shared-checkout:452 runs `git -C "$target" rev-parse --show-toplevel` with `$target` taken from the inspected command, including on segments the real command would never execute (e.g. the right side of a short-circuiting `&&`). The argument is quoted so there is no shell injection, but git does read that directory's config. No privilege boundary is crossed — the session was already about to run git there and already has a shell — so the delta is close to nil.

Supply-chain delta of the tracked PreToolUse hook, judged as configured: the committed file names exactly one fixed command (a tracked script under `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/`), ships no `permissions` key, and `timeout: 10` and `$comment` change nothing about what executes. The real delta is that a committer's reach moves from model-mediated (`.claude/commands/*.md` prose) to unmediated code execution on every collaborator's host before every Bash call, including the orchestrator host outside the mika#2141 sandbox. That trade-off is named in the file and in CONTRIBUTING and is the point of the change; what is NOT bounded is future drift of that file, which is filed as finding 2.
Callsite completeness for 'nothing else in the repo reads MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT / MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT_LOG': grep-only (no symbol-aware or AST search available for shell).
testing_gaps: scripts/test-guard-shared-checkout.sh asserts the deny and bypass log lines exist (AC5/AC6, lines 258 and 271) but never asserts what they must NOT contain. A positive/negative pair — feed a command carrying `ghp_...`, `GH_TOKEN=...` and a `https://user:token@host` remote, assert the literal secret is absent from the log while the `deny project=/target=/verb=` fields survive — is the assertion whose absence let finding 1 ship.

No test covers the log file's mode or the `${MIKA_HOME:-${HOME:-/tmp}/.mika}` default path resolution; every test exports MIKA_GUARD_SHARED_CHECKOUT_LOG to a temp file (test-guard-shared-checkout.sh:103), so the production default is exercised by nothing.

scripts/test-check-shared-checkout-guard-wiring.sh has no negative fixture for a settings.json that keeps the guard hook AND adds a second hook command or a top-level `env` block — the two shapes finding 2 describes both pass the current gate, so the gate's own blind spot is untested.
